tasks.short: File forms, schedule, and proofread letters.

steps.what: File official forms into the records screen.
Schedule appointments on the open calendar.
Proofread correspondence before it is sent.

loop.input: the clerk's points and the letter template
loop.check: every date and case id matches the register
loop.stop: stop when the letter has no case id
loop.why_not_simpler: wording of an official letter is not a mail-merge of fixed cells

steps.what: Take dictation when the official will not type.

tasks.design: Official forms file into {WORKFLOW} when every required box is filled, and open slots on {CALENDAR} become appointments. Correspondence is proofread against the register before the clerk sends it. Dictation stays with the clerk when an official will not type. A letter with no case id is not sent. No new recording of the official's voice is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: Forms, the diary, and outgoing letters were three piles, and a wrong date was caught by the recipient.
tasks.enabler_now: A form with required boxes and a calendar with open slots can be filed and booked. The letter still needs a person.
tasks.still_hard: Officials still dictate, and a letter can say something the template should not say.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears when a sentence would commit the court to a date the register does not hold.
tasks.altitude: Filing and booking take less of the morning. Dictation and the decision to send a letter stay with the clerk.

reach.task: Schedule an appointment and file the form that belongs to it.
reach.learn: A slot can be booked from the calendar. Sending an official letter still needs this clerk.

evidence.claim: A form with required fields can be stored, and an open calendar slot can be booked. A letter still needs a person to match it to the case.
The job digest says works-council consent is required before call recording. This task uses the clerk's notes, not a new recording. Sending the letter is the clerk's act.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Form type, case or party id, and appointment date, produced by the submitted form or the official's request. A letter must carry a case id from the register. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing form screen and calendar before adding a new diary.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Who may send a letter besides this clerk.
research_questions: What share of letters are template plus a case id?
Which forms fail the required-field check today?

already_counted.description: The clerk still proofreads and accepts the letter.

incremental.description: The clerk updates a letter template when the court changes a sentence.

approvals.approved_version: case id and the letter text shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If officials still dictate most letters, the clerk's time stays and the saving is near the low end. Template letters with a case id keep the high end.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Question applicants and record their answers.

steps.what: Open the prescribed forms with required fields.
Question applicants for name, address, and age.
Record only answers the applicant confirmed.

tasks.design: The prescribed form opens in {WORKFLOW} with the required fields and nothing else. The registry clerk questions the applicant and records only answers the person confirmed. The form does not decide whether the applicant qualifies. A field the person did not confirm stays empty and the clerk finishes it later.
tasks.previous_blocker: Clerks asked from memory and wrote on paper forms that did not match the current prescription.
tasks.enabler_now: The prescribed fields can sit on the screen. The conversation cannot be skipped.
tasks.still_hard: People do not have a document for every field, and age or address can be sensitive to ask in a public room.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk sees when an applicant does not understand the question, and stops rather than guessing an answer.
tasks.altitude: The form no longer asks for fields the prescription dropped. The questioning stays the clerk's conversation. Nothing about qualification is decided here.

reach.task: Interview an applicant and record the answers the form requires.
reach.learn: Record what was said. Do not turn the answers into a grant or a refusal on this desk.

evidence.claim: A prescribed form can show the required fields. It cannot conduct the interview.

The job digest says benefit eligibility is high-risk and a solely automated decision with legal effect needs a legal ground. This task only records confirmed answers. It does not refuse anyone. No emotion recognition is used.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Form id and the prescribed field names, produced by the form catalogue. Name, address, and age are recorded only after the applicant confirms them. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the existing application form before designing a new one.
Any edit after approval voids the version and returns the item to the clerk.
unknowns: Which fields the current prescription requires.
Whether a private room is available for the questions.
research_questions: Which fields are usually unconfirmed at the counter?

already_counted.description: The clerk still questions the applicant.
The clerk still records the confirmed answers.

incremental.description: The clerk updates the prescribed field list when the form changes.

approvals.approved_version: form id and the confirmed answers shown to the clerk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The interview is almost the whole task. Saving is only the blank form and a shorter write-up, and it falls further if many answers stay unconfirmed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Instruct parties about court appearance times.

steps.what: Show the court appearance time from the calendar.
Instruct parties about that timing by phone.
Note what the party was told about timing.

tasks.design: The {CALENDAR} shows the appearance time for the case. The registry clerk instructs the party by phone or at the counter, in the words the party can follow. The screen does not call the party. The clerk notes what was said. A case with two times on the calendar is not instructed until the clerk picks the live one.
tasks.previous_blocker: Appearance times were read from a paper list that went stale during the day.
tasks.enabler_now: The live calendar can show one time. Explaining it to a worried party stays a conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Parties miss the point of a time, and a changed hearing may not be on the card yet.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk notices when a party has not understood, and says it again in plainer words.
tasks.altitude: The clerk no longer hunts the time. The instruction, and the choice to say it again, stay with the clerk.

reach.task: Give a caller the fact they need and stay on the line until they have it.
reach.learn: A time can be read from a screen. Staying with the party until they understand stays human.

evidence.claim: A calendar can show one appearance time. It cannot tell whether the party understood.
A machine must not place this call. The job digest says a machine chat must identify itself, and this instruction is the clerk speaking. No recording is added.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Case id and a single appearance time, produced by the court calendar. If two times are present, the step stops. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Read the time from the existing calendar before building a reminder campaign.
unknowns: Whether parties expect a call or a letter.
Which language the counter can speak.
research_questions: How often does the calendar show two times for one case?
What share of parties miss the appearance today?

already_counted.description: The clerk still instructs the party.
The clerk still notes what was said.

incremental.description: The clerk checks that reminder wording still matches the calendar.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The phone call is most of the task. Saving is the lookup only, and it shrinks when the calendar often shows two times and the clerk must resolve them.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Answer calls, file documents, and keep supplies.

steps.what: Place filed court documents in the case folder.
Answer telephone calls about today's list.
Maintain office supplies and the counter equipment.

tasks.design: Court documents with a case id land in the right folder in {DOCS}. Telephone calls about today's list stay with the registry clerk, who answers them. Supplies and counter equipment stay a walk around the office. The screen does not answer the phone and does not order supplies on its own. A document with no case id waits for the clerk.
tasks.previous_blocker: Filing, the phone, and a supply cupboard were one interrupted morning, with no split between them.
tasks.enabler_now: A document with a case id can be filed without a phone call. The call itself cannot.
tasks.still_hard: Callers do not have a case number, and a jammed counter machine is physical.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk hears which call is a party in distress and which is a simple time question.
tasks.altitude: Clear documents file themselves into the case. The phone and the cupboard stay the clerk's. The week does not become a monitored call score.

reach.task: Accept an item and place it where the address says.
reach.learn: A case id can place a document. A telephone conversation cannot be placed that way.

evidence.claim: A document with a case id can be stored in the case folder. Answering a telephone and refilling a cupboard cannot.
The job digest says agent dashboards and call recording need works-council consent. This task adds neither. The clerk answers the phone.

assumptions: Workflow boundary: The desk is a European municipal court registry and licensing counter. The sentence uses US public-sector wording and is read as the local court, council, or permit this municipality actually issues.

Fields: Case id and document type, produced by the filing stamp or the register. A document without a case id is not filed by the screen. If a required field is missing, the step stops and the clerk finishes it by hand.
Native check: Use the case folder that already exists before adding a second store.
The supply step names the counter equipment in plain words. No vendor is assumed.
unknowns: What share of documents arrive without a case id.
research_questions: How many calls are only about today's list?
Which counter machines fail in a typical week?

already_counted.description: The clerk still answers the telephone.
The clerk still keeps supplies and equipment.

incremental.description: The clerk adds a document type when the court introduces one.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The phone is most of the hour. Filing a few clear documents is the saving, and it disappears in a week when almost every paper lacks a case id.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The clerk still questions applicants, instructs parties, and answers the phone. Form filing, appointment slots, and routine proofreading leave the hour.
reach: Loan interviewers ask for the fields a form requires, and this desk learns that the interview itself stays a conversation.
Medical secretaries schedule from a calendar, and this desk learns which court time still needs the clerk to say it aloud.
skills_to_grow: Ask only for the fields the prescribed form lists, and stop when the person has not confirmed an answer.
Tell a letter that can be proofread against a template from one the official must dictate.
role.ambitious_version: An applicant with a complete form is recorded the same visit, and the questions the form does not ask still wait for the clerk.
